judge_verdict.summary: Near-complete adaptability run (11/12 oracle actions) but the outbound email misreported which properties were saved, so the verifier's FAIL is fair.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a fair verifier rejection of a near-miss: the GAIA2 adaptability verifier scored binary_reward 0 with continuous reward 0.916667 (11/12 oracle write-actions matched) [1], gating pass on a perfect 1.0 action-match fraction in adaptability mode [2]. The user task required finding the lowest-violent-crime location, saving unsaved properties there, emailing all contact data scientists about what was saved, notifying the user, and adapting to change requests via Messages [3]; the reference oracle performs twelve write actions ending in unsaving three sub-$1500 listings and messaging Kritsana [4]. The agent correctly identified Liege zip 4000 (violent crime 4.69) as the lowest among checked locations [5], found both data scientists (Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda) [6], and saved the same six previously-unsaved Liege apartment IDs the oracle saves [7]. However, its successful email to those recipients listed nine Liege properties—including Liege Loft, Liege Luxury, and Liege Living that were already marked saved before the agent acted—rather than the six it had just saved, with a different subject and body than the oracle's single consolidated email [8]; that semantic mismatch is the plausible 1/12 oracle-action failure behind the 0.916667 score. The agent did notify the user that the email was sent [9] and correctly handled Kritsana's reply by removing the three sub-€1500 saved apartments and sending a Messages update [10], but the email-content defect means it did not fully accomplish the task as specified, so verifier FAIL and not-truly-solved align as TN rather than FN [8][10].

evidence.claim: The user task requires saving unsaved low-crime properties, emailing all data-scientist contacts with prices and locations, notifying the user when sent, and handling change requests on Messages.

citations.quote: Find the location with the lowest violent crime rate and save any unsaved properties there. Send one email to all the data scientists in my contacts, informing them that I have saved the properties they requested with the prices and locations, let me know when you send the email. If anyone wants some changes done, address their request and message them on Messages to let them know of the changes.

evidence.claim: The reference oracle performs twelve write actions: six saves, one email to both data scientists, user notification, three unsaves after an ENV reply, and a Messages update to Kritsana.
The agent determined Liege (zip 4000) had the lowest violent crime rate among locations it checked (4.69).

citations.quote: Liege has the lowest violent-crime rate found, so I'll retrieve its listings.

evidence.claim: The agent identified exactly two data-scientist contacts and emailed both at the correct addresses.

citations.quote: I found two exact data scientists. Now I'll inspect rental listings and saved properties.

evidence.claim: The agent saved the same six previously-unsaved Liege apartment IDs that the oracle saves.

The agent's successful email listed nine Liege properties (including three already saved before its save actions) with subject 'Saved Liege properties', diverging from the oracle email that lists only the six newly saved properties under subject 'Saved Properties as Requested'.

- Liege Luxe
